title: The paper-plane Scrum simulation - velocity, estimation, and what actually goes wrong in a sprint

resources_seen.slides_note: NO SLIDE DECK in resources/. The game rules, the acceptance criteria and the Assignment 2 brief and rubric were all shown on screen but not distributed. Everything in the notes is reconstructed from speech.
resources_seen.transcript_quality: poor - workshop audio. Roughly lines 165-235 and 425-465 are near-total noise. The lecturer's framed segments (rules, reviews, debrief, Assignment 2 brief) are intact; student contributions are patchy and partly reconstructed from context.
resources_seen.figures_note: No deck and no visual material to rasterise. All diagrams and tables in L4-notes.md are generated (CLAUDE.md 3.3a fallback).

concepts.name: The simulation: rules, story-point mapping, timeboxes, acceptance criteria
concepts.source: transcript - rules walkthrough and sprint-2 requirements announcement
concepts.note: Untested. The game rules themselves are a teaching device, not examinable. What is quizzable: 1 plane = 1 story point, velocity = planes accepted, and the fact that one acceptance criterion (aesthetics) was subjective and PO-owned.

concepts.name: Estimation accuracy beats raw velocity
concepts.source: transcript - sprint 1 and 2 reviews, results debrief
concepts.note: Untested. The debrief's headline finding. Sprint 1 figures are complete (A 3->1, B 3->2, C 3->2, D 8->3); sprint 2 is only partially recoverable and the notes mark the gaps. Do NOT cite a number for Team A in sprint 2 - the transcript contains two conflicting statements.

concepts.name: Sprint length is never altered
concepts.note: Untested. Note the nuance the notes draw out: the sprint BOUNDARY is the invariant; internal event timeboxes were in fact altered on the fly, which is why sprint 1 and 2 velocities here are not strictly comparable.

concepts.name: Requirements changed mid-project, on purpose
concepts.note: Untested. Legitimate change: stated business reason, additive, extra resources attached. Pairs directly with L3-C06.

concepts.name: Understanding the requirements is every member's job
concepts.source: transcript - Team C sprint 2 review and debrief
concepts.note: Untested. Cleanest lesson in the lecture. The diagnosis is structural, not carelessness - it is the L3-C10 inspection pillar failing. Explicitly NOT delegated to the Scrum Master.

concepts.name: Test in something that resembles production
concepts.source: transcript - sprint 2 review, debrief, Team B's retrospective contribution
concepts.note: Untested. Everyone tested that the plane flew; nobody tested that they could hit the target. Different rigs, second inferred from the first. Sibling of the Code Runner trap in L3-C08.

concepts.name: Self-organising teams switch roles between sprints
concepts.source: transcript - debrief, Team B and Team D retrospective accounts
concepts.note: Untested. Team B dissolved a dedicated QA role that was the wrong shape for a 5-minute sprint and recovered the aesthetics criterion. Evidence for the L3-C09 claim.

concepts.name: Converge on one design
concepts.note: Untested. One design, at most two. The reconciliation with Team A's explore-then-optimise defence is the actual lesson: explore in sprint 1, converge by sprint 2. Real-project analogue is technology/architecture choice.

concepts.name: Onboarding a late or returning member costs sprint time
concepts.note: Untested. Two obligations: catch them up, and get them productive rather than merely informed. Cheaper if everyone has a designated backup (L3-C13).

concepts.name: The retrospective is the mechanism, not a debrief
concepts.source: transcript - between-sprints ordering correction and collective debrief
concepts.note: Untested. Retrospective BEFORE the next planning session, because its output is that session's input. The lecturer corrected himself live on this.

concepts.name: Everyone is a leader and there is no leader - in practice
concepts.note: Untested. Assignment 2 material. The honest cost of flat structure is the consensus problem; the four-designs failure (L4-C08) IS a consensus failure. SM verb list: looking, reviewing, tracking, monitoring - never decide/assign/approve.

concepts.name: The Product Owner is part of the system too
concepts.note: Untested. Two admitted PO mistakes materially affected velocity. The transferable claim: a retrospective's target is the whole system, not just the team's own behaviour. 'Pilot error' = a defect in the demo, not the product.
